name: umich-dining-mcp

tools.name: list_locations
tools.description: List the ten University of Michigan dining halls with their address, phone, e-mail, map link, the service periods published for the requested day, whether they are serving right now, and whether they have a gluten-free pantry. Cafes, markets, bakeries, grills, prices and meal plans are out of scope.

date.description: The day to read. Defaults to today.

tools.name: get_menu
tools.description: Get the menu of one dining hall: meals, stations and dishes, with each dish's traits (the six boolean ones as codes), its allergens as codes, its nutrient-density tier, its carbon footprint tier, its calories and its serving size. Read the "key" block to resolve the codes and the "fields" list to read a row, which is an array. The full nutrition panel of a single dish comes from get_item_nutrition. The date defaults to today; the site publishes menus for today-3 days to today+14 days. Allergen data is only as good as the site. The menu page flags the allergens the kitchen reported for a dish, but the data does not distinguish "contains" from "may contain", there are no ingredient lists, and it is not safe to treat a missing flag as an absence of the allergen. The site's own guidance is: "Look for the signs posted near each food serving area for a list of menu options with allergens highlighted in red." The "Gluten Free" trait means the dish is made without gluten, not that it is safe for someone with coeliac disease. Dedicated gluten-free pantries exist only at South Quad, East Quad, Mosher-Jordan and Bursley.

date.description: The day to read. Defaults to today.

limit.description: How many dishes to return. The whole menu is returned when it is not given.

include_nutrients.description: The nutrients to return, by canonical key or by published name, or ["all"].

tools.name: search_dishes
tools.description: Search dish names across the dining halls, or within the halls that are named. The match is a case-insensitive substring match on the dish name. A single day is searched by default; "from" and "to" search a range of days, and each row then lists the days the dish appeared on. The rows carry codes: read key.halls, key.meals, key.stations, key.traits and key.allergens to resolve them. The rows are arrays: the "fields" list names the positions, in order. The row always carries the calories and the serving size; every other nutrient, the sodium included, is asked for with include_nutrients. mhealthyTier is 1 (Nutrient Dense Low) to 5 (Nutrient Dense High) and carbonFootprint is 1 (low), 2 (medium) or 3 (high). The rows are returned in the order asked for, and "limit" takes the first of them: the default is 50.

query.description: Text to look for in the dish names.

hall.description: The halls to search: one hall, or a list of them. Leave it out, or pass an empty list, for every hall.

date.description: A single day to search. Cannot be combined with from/to.

from.description: The first day of a range to search.

to.description: The last day of a range to search. Defaults to the last published day.

offset.description: How many pages of the range to skip. The response names the offset of the next page.

include_nutrients.description: The nutrients to return, by canonical key or by published name, or ["all"].

sort_by.description: The field to sort on, e.g. "calories" or "protein". The default order is by hall, meal and name.

sort_order.description: The direction of the sort. The default is descending.

limit.description: How many rows to return, the first of them in the order asked for. Defaults to 50; ask again with a larger limit for more.

tools.name: filter_dishes
tools.description: Filter the dining hall menus by allergen, trait, nutrient density, carbon footprint and nutrients. exclude_allergens removes dishes that carry any of the listed allergens; require_traits keeps only dishes that carry every listed trait; min_mhealthy is the lowest acceptable nutrient-density tier (3 = Nutrient Dense Medium or better); max_carbon is the highest acceptable carbon footprint (1 = low, 2 = medium, 3 = high). Both of them drop the dishes the site did not tag: a dish with no nutrient density is not "dense", and a dish with no carbon footprint does not pass a carbon cap. max_calories and min_calories and the sodium bounds are numeric caps that exclude dishes without published values. nutrients takes a range per nutrient, e.g. {"protein": {"min": 20, "unit": "g"}}; the unit defaults to the nutrient's own and is checked. A micronutrient threshold without a unit is read in the amount the row carries: {"Iron": {"min": 2}} means 2 mg of iron, while {"Iron": {"min": 2, "unit": "%DV"}} means 2 percent of the Daily Value. include_nutrients names the nutrients to return; it defaults to the ones the filter used, and a nutrient the filter constrained is always returned. The row always carries the calories and the serving size; every other nutrient, the sodium included, is asked for by name. A single day is filtered by default; "from" and "to" filter a range and each row then lists the days the dish appeared on. The rows carry codes: read key.halls, key.meals, key.stations, key.traits and key.allergens to resolve them, and the "fields" list to read a row. Allergen data is only as good as the site. The menu page flags the allergens the kitchen reported for a dish, but the data does not distinguish "contains" from "may contain", there are no ingredient lists, and it is not safe to treat a missing flag as an absence of the allergen. The site's own guidance is: "Look for the signs posted near each food serving area for a list of menu options with allergens highlighted in red." The "Gluten Free" trait means the dish is made without gluten, not that it is safe for someone with coeliac disease. Dedicated gluten-free pantries exist only at South Quad, East Quad, Mosher-Jordan and Bursley.

exclude_allergens.description: Keeps only the dishes that carry none of these allergens.

require_traits.description: Keeps only the dishes that carry every one of these traits.

min_mhealthy.description: The lowest acceptable nutrient-density tier. The dishes the site did not tag are dropped.

max_carbon.description: The highest acceptable carbon footprint: 1 (low), 2 (medium) or 3 (high). The dishes the site did not tag are dropped.

max_calories.description: The highest acceptable number of calories.

min_calories.description: The lowest acceptable number of calories.

max_sodium_mg.description: The highest acceptable amount of sodium, in mg.

min_sodium_mg.description: The lowest acceptable amount of sodium, in mg.

nutrients.description: A range per nutrient, e.g. {"protein": {"min": 20, "unit": "g"}}. A constraint on a nutrient excludes the dishes that publish no value for it.

min.description: The lowest acceptable value, in the unit below.

max.description: The highest acceptable value, in the unit below.

unit.description: The unit of the bounds. It defaults to the nutrient's own; a micronutrient defaults to the published percent.

include_nutrients.description: The nutrients to return, by canonical key or by published name, or ["all"].

query.description: A case-insensitive substring of the dish name.

sort_by.description: The field to sort on: a nutrient key (calories, sodium, protein, totalFat, …), a micronutrient name (Iron, Calcium, …), or one of proteinToCalorie and fiberToCalorie. An unknown field is refused.

sort_order.description: The direction of the sort. It defaults to desc, so the biggest value comes first.

hall.description: The halls to search: one hall, or a list of them. Leave it out, or pass an empty list, for every hall.

date.description: A single day to filter. Cannot be combined with from/to.

from.description: The first day of a range to filter.

to.description: The last day of a range to filter. Defaults to the last published day.

offset.description: How many pages of the range to skip. The response names the offset of the next page.

limit.description: How many rows to return, the first of them in the order asked for. Defaults to 50; ask again with a larger limit for more.

tools.name: list_nutrition_fields
tools.description: List the canonical nutrient identifiers, their units, the alternative units a threshold may be written in, and the Daily Value basis of the published micronutrients. A constraint on a nutrient excludes the dishes that publish no value for it, and a value the site writes as "trace" or "< 1%" is missing rather than zero.

tools.name: get_hours
tools.description: Get the service periods published for a dining hall on the requested day, together with the hall's regular weekly schedule. Without a hall argument every hall is returned. A hall that cannot be read is reported in the failures and the other halls are still returned.

date.description: The day to read. Defaults to today.

tools.name: find_open_now
tools.description: Return the dining halls that are serving at the given time of day, and the ones that are not, with the service periods of the day. Without arguments the current campus-local time is used.

date.description: The day to look at. Defaults to today.

at.description: The campus-local time of day to look at. Defaults to the current time.

tools.name: get_item_nutrition
tools.description: Get the full nutrition panel of one dish, including the serving size, calories, the fat, cholesterol, sodium, carbohydrate and protein values and the micronutrients. The dish name is matched case-insensitively; an exact match wins, otherwise a unique substring match is used and an ambiguous name is reported rather than guessed. Allergen data is only as good as the site. The menu page flags the allergens the kitchen reported for a dish, but the data does not distinguish "contains" from "may contain", there are no ingredient lists, and it is not safe to treat a missing flag as an absence of the allergen. The site's own guidance is: "Look for the signs posted near each food serving area for a list of menu options with allergens highlighted in red." The "Gluten Free" trait means the dish is made without gluten, not that it is safe for someone with coeliac disease. Dedicated gluten-free pantries exist only at South Quad, East Quad, Mosher-Jordan and Bursley.

date.description: Calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD. The site publishes menus for today-3 days to today+14 days.

meal.description: Narrow the search to one meal.

station.description: Narrow the search to one station.

instructions: Menus, hours, traits and nutrition for the dining halls of the University of Michigan, read from the public site at dining.umich.edu. This server is not affiliated with or endorsed by the university, and the data is unofficial: the site is the only authority, and its allergen flags are advisory. The rows of the sweep tools carry codes; read the "key" block of the response to resolve them.
